name: Main valley debris flow
description: The debris flow of the main valley: the forested stream from the northern hills was scoured into a channel 30-60 m wide over 1.3 km, and it dumped a fan of boulders, sand and logs at the head of Tha Byar, where January's image shows forest and orchards.

name: North-west tributary flow
description: A tributary from the north-west hills scoured into a wide braided bed of sand and gravel that joins the main valley flow at the north edge of the survey.

name: Long slide
description: A 500 m open-slope failure on the east face of the ridge: it broke away at about 165 m and ran north-east down to the floor of the main valley, stripping the forest to bare soil.

name: West-bank slide
description: Slope failure on the west bank of the debris fan, whose debris slid east into the fan above the village.

name: Southern debris flow
description: A debris flow that enters the survey from the south-west as a broad braided deposit, bends north-east and runs east along a scoured channel into the southern part of the village.

name: North-spur channel network
description: Branching channels scoured down the north side of the spur west of the valley, draining east along a gully that joins the main valley flow.

name: West-edge channel
description: A channel scoured down the west edge of the survey that spread sand among the trees where the spur's southern channels meet, above the southern debris flow.

name: Ridge gullies
description: Gullies scoured down the east face of the ridge beside the long slide.

name: Twin channels
description: Two parallel channels scoured down the west flank of the spur.

name: Spur slide
description: Open-slope failure on the south flank of the spur.

name: Spur chute
description: Narrow debris chute on the south flank of the spur.

name: North-west edge channel
description: Channel scoured at the north-west edge of the survey.

name: West-edge gully
description: Gully scoured at the west edge of the survey.

name: South-west channel
description: Scoured channel near the south-west edge of the survey.

name: Scar beside the long slide
description: Small open-slope scar beside the toe of the long slide.

name: West river channel
description: The largest scoured channel: a stream bed stripped to sand and boulders from the south-west hills to the north edge of the survey, with its south-east tributary.

name: North-west channels
description: Tributary channels in young plantation west of the monastery, scoured and buried in sand.

name: Central channel
description: A forested stream scoured from the foot of the southern hill north to the monastery road.

name: South channel network
description: The east-west stream at the foot of the southern hill and the branch that comes down to it from the south.

name: Road slide
description: The largest open-slope failure: a stepped scar in red soil below the pagoda hill whose debris reached the road.

name: South edge scar
description: Open-slope scar at the southern edge of the survey; its upper part lies beyond the flight.

name: Plantation flow
description: Debris flow through a plantation down to the road east of the monastery.

name: Curving slide
description: Slide east of the pagoda whose debris curved north-east around a grass field.

name: West branch channel
description: Scoured side channel joining the west river channel.

name: South-west gully

name: Main valley debris flow
description: The large debris flow of the valley: an amphitheatre-shaped source scar and the scoured stream channel west of it fed one flow that cut a corridor through the middle of Ka Det Nge Htein, where houses and the road stood in January.

name: West chute
description: Narrow debris slide off the east flank of the KD-01 amphitheatre, running into the main channel.

name: Long chute
description: The longest open-slope chute on the north wall of the valley, ending on the debris fan above the corridor.

name: Twin scar
description: Two scars side by side on the north wall - a narrow upper one and a wide lower one - whose debris merged.

name: Slide onto the old clearing
description: Forest slope that failed onto a clearing already bare in January 2026 (the clearing itself is excluded).

name: North-east gully
description: Debris flow scoured down a forested gully towards the north end of the village.

name: North tip slide
description: Open-slope slide at the northern tip of the survey, high on the ridge.

name: North gully track
description: Narrow scour track in a forested gully on the upper slope.

name: South gully track
description: Debris track along the stream on the south side of the valley, ending above the school.

name: Northern debris-flood fan
description: Debris flood / mudflow deposit; feeder channel enters from the west outside the survey, LS-02 runout also drains into it

name: Narrow northern debris flow
description: Long narrow scar on forested slope; channelised runout to the north-east into LS-01

name: Twin-scar debris flow, north village
description: Two adjoining scars merging into one runout that buried the west side of the northern village and reached the road between houses

name: Stream-channel debris flow
description: Channelised debris flow down a stream with two tributary scars; scoured the bed and reached the road

name: Hillslope slide to road
description: Short slide reaching the road from the west

name: Narrow central debris flow
description: Long narrow scar; runout reached the road and joins the LS-07 fan

name: Central debris-flow complex
description: Largest event: wide scoured source zone, runout through the village road and a fan across the paddies

name: Long southern debris flow
description: Long scar and channel; runout crossed the road junction into the paddies

name: Southern slope failure
description: Broad shallow failure of the forested slope at the south edge of the survey; continues beyond the flown area
